You have Atlassian MCP tools available but DEFERRED. First run ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page" and max_results 2 to load the schema.

Then read Confluence page ID 256835585 — "Technical Solution Design – PWA" IN FULL (convert_to_markdown=true, include_metadata=true). It is a long architecture document.

Context: I am researching the CONSENT position for a "Recently Viewed products" feature that stores a shopper's product browsing history — session-only for guests, account-persisted for logged-in shoppers — on the Zimmermann SFCC PWA storefront. Another Confluence page ("04.6 Consent Management — Business Overview") points at "TSD: §11 Consent & Marketing" for the technical implementation, so §11 is the priority.

Report:
- The page's version number (from metadata) and the "Last updated" date stated in the body.
- Section 11 "Consent & Marketing" (or whatever the consent section is actually numbered — report its real number and title) reproduced COMPLETELY AND VERBATIM.
- Any other passage anywhere in the document mentioning: Didomi, consent, cookies, GDPR/CCPA/privacy, tracking, personalisation, browsing history, "Recently Viewed", localStorage/sessionStorage, data retention, or Einstein/recommendations. Quote verbatim with the section number it appears under.
- Explicitly state whether the document mentions "Recently Viewed" at all.
- Explicitly state whether ANY data retention period is specified anywhere in the document.
- Explicitly state whether it distinguishes guest vs authenticated/logged-in shopper treatment for stored data or consent.
- Note any per-region consent differences (AU vs EU/UK vs US vs HK/ME) and any Didomi purpose/category names or purpose IDs mentioned.
- Note any "TBC"/open-item markers near consent content, quoting them.

Quote verbatim; do not paraphrase. Do NOT modify anything — read-only. Do not write any files. Return findings as your final message.

138|This project uses the Salesforce PWA Kit's *template extensibility* model. `@salesforce/retail-react-app` is consumed as an unmodified npm dependency, not a forked copy of the repository.
139|
140|All customisations live in an `overrides/` directory that mirrors the structure of the underlying `@salesforce/retail-react-app` package. The base package is consumed unmodified — overrides take precedence at resolution time. This keeps the project upgradeable: pulling a new Salesforce baseline is a dependency bump plus a targeted reconciliation of overridden files, not a full re-application of patches.
141|
142|**Working principle:** stay as close to base PWA Kit behaviour as possible. Visual changes (Chakra props, theme tokens, SCSS where Chakra is insufficient) are expected. Structural changes (data flow, routing, or layout deviations from the base template) are taken deliberately and reviewed against the upgrade impact before being merged.

340|### 8.4 Structured data
341|
342|Custom JSON-LD per the Sparro templates, rendered server-side so crawlers see it on the first response:
343|
344|* **PDP:** Product + Merchant Listing Schema (`ProductGroup` + variant `Product`s), with real-time inventory driving availability.
345|* **PLP:** CollectionPage + BreadcrumbList + ItemList Schema (ItemList reflects the initial SSR'd product batch).
346|* **Boutique pages:** LocalBusiness / ClothingStore Schema per location.
347|* **Homepages:** Organisation + WebSite Schema per regional storefront, with per-prefix `WebSite` nodes (including the Global-e international paths `/en-ca/` and `/en-ch/`).
348|
349|### 8.5 URL strategy
350|
351|* Product URL: `/[prefix]/[name]-[colour].html` — the `.html` suffix is preserved to maintain existing indexed URLs.
352|* Category URL: `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no suffix), with 301 redirects from legacy paths.
353|* 301 redirects for every URL that changes as a result of migration (products, categories, content). Implemented at the CDN/edge layer to keep application-layer impact minimal.
354|
355|### 8.6 GEO (DMU-042)
356|
357|No GEO-specific features in launch scope. The technical foundations enabling post-launch GEO — SSR, structured data, canonicals, XML sitemaps — are in place at go-live so no architecture decision blocks future activation.
358|

361|9. Performance Strategy
362|-----------------------
363|
364|LCP at p75 mobile is the binding constraint and the de-facto cap on third-party script weight.
365|
366|| Metric | Target |
367|| --- | --- |
368|| LCP (mobile p75) | ≤ 2 s |
369|| Lighthouse Performance | ≥ 0.80 |
370|| Lighthouse Accessibility | ≥ 0.90 |
371|| Lighthouse Best Practices | ≥ 0.90 |
372|
373|### 9.1 Third-party defer rule
374|
375|Anything loaded via Didomi callback (GTM — which loads Meta, GA4, and other GTM-housed tags via Tell No Lies; Narvar EDD widget; Inside Chat) is deferred, async-loaded, or injected post-hydration so it does not block LCP. **Measmerize** (Find My Size / size guide — PDP only) likewise defers behind LCP — the script injects after the product hero image has loaded. **reCAPTCHA** likewise loads only on register/login form interaction, so it never sits on the critical path of any other page (consent treatment per §11.1). **Exception (AAB-004):** Optimizely Web is a PWA-direct head tag (not a GTM tag) and deliberately loads in the page head **before render** to prevent A/B flicker, scoped to the US storefront where Optimizely runs. **Crazy Egg (AAB-005)** loads async and post-Didomi-consent. Both load strictly post-Didomi-consent; keep both snippets minimal.
376|
377|### 9.2 Other levers
378|
379|* **Images:** all storefront imagery — product and editorial — is stored in and served from **Contentful** (`images.ctfassets.net`) via the Contentful Images API; SFCC holds no image assets (DMU-010 migration de-scoped; product images CRM-075; all media via the CMS library HPC-003). The PWA generates `srcset` / `sizes` and sets size, quality, and format per breakpoint on the asset URL — **AVIF primary with WebP / JPEG fallbacks**. Lazy-load all non-LCP images; priority-load the primary hero image (PRD-064). Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
380|* **Video:** sourced by platform, not self-hosted, so codec / adaptive-streaming selection belongs to the upstream player rather than to this layer:
381|
382|  + **Product videos → Vimeo**, referenced by embed URL stored in product data or the CMS (PRD-067). Load behind a lightweight facade (poster image + click/scroll-to-load) so the Vimeo player JS never lands on the LCP critical path.
383|  + **Content-managed page videos → Contentful** by default, served from the Contentful asset CDN and referenced within the CMS content entry alongside the page content. Editorial pages may also embed a Vimeo video by URL where preferred (HPC-004) — the product/editorial split above is the expected pattern, not a hard restriction.
384|  + Across both: `preload="metadata"` by default; autoplay reserved for muted, short-loop hero clips only.
385|* Dynamic imports for heavy non-initial components.
386|* Parallel data fetches; no client-side waterfalls. Fetch only required fields.

389|
390|The CI Lighthouse gate (§14.3) catches regressions but runs against the Dev-tier MRT deployment — slower than production hardware, further from the edge, and not representative of the LCP a real shopper experiences. The signed-off LCP and Lighthouse targets in this section are therefore validated against **Stage**, which mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier). Treat CI numbers as regression indicators; treat Stage numbers as the contractual ones.

The first Stage performance run should include per-pool queue-depth and connection-wait metrics (undici emits these as diagnostic channel events). Use those numbers to validate or revise the caps.

455|12. Graceful Degradation
456|------------------------
457|
458|Each external system fails independently — one outage does not break a page.
459|
460|| System | Failure mode |
461|| --- | --- |
462|| Contentful | Render page without editorial content; never block commerce data on CMS |
463|| Global-e | Surface explicit error; do not silently fall back to SFCC for international checkout |
464|| Didomi | Fail closed — no consent, no third-party scripts |
465|| Omneo (writes) / Emarsys | Queue and retry silently; never block the user flow |
466|| Omneo (reads) | **Load-bearing for My Account profile pages** — per DMU-004 only email + Omneo ID are migrated; all other customer profile data is sourced live from Omneo at login. Surface an explicit retry/error UI on profile pages if the round-trip fails; do not render stale or partial profile data. |
467|| Google Maps | Degrade to manual address entry; never hard-block checkout |
468|| AP21 (Retail Rewards) | On AP21 unavailability at the point of Rewards application, inform the customer and allow an alternative payment method |
469|| Narvar (EDD) | Suppress widget; do not show an error or block checkout |
470|
471|### 12.1 Blast-Radius Containment
472|
473|The failure modes above describe what the PWA does when a single integration is unavailable. This section covers how to limit the *spread* of an attack or outage — ensuring a degraded integration cannot consume shared resources and take down unrelated features.
474|
475|#### Edge (outside the PWA — Infrastructure / SI Partner)
476|
477|* **Web Application Firewalls + rate limiting** is the primary lever for volumetric attacks and credential-stuffing.
478|* **SFCC Business Manager** provides API-level rate limiting for SFCC endpoints, independent of the storefront edge.
479|
480|#### SSR layer (inside the PWA)
481|
482|`overrides/app/ssr.js` makes server-side `fetch` calls directly (token exchange, JWKS, SF Payments metadata). Node's native `fetch` is backed by `undici` internally. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).
483|
484|> **Implementation note:** the per-call `dispatcher` option is safer than the `setGlobalDispatcher` in a managed environment (MRT) since it does not touch the global dispatcher that Salesforce internal libraries may rely on. The `commerce-sdk-react` hooks manage their own HTTP client server-side (Commerce SDK) and are not affected in either approach.
485|
486|The connection pool split is an engineering decision — the right pool boundaries and sizes depend on observed traffic patterns and the integration map in §7. Planned pools (connection caps should be validated later — see §9.3):
487|
488|| Pool | Origin | Calls | Cap | `connectTimeout` | `bodyTimeout` | Reasoning |
489|| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
490|| `sfcc-scapi` | `<https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`> | SLAS JWKS (token validation for passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 8 s | `jose` caches the JWK set for its rotation period; actual network calls are rare. Isolated so a JWKS fetch is never starved by higher-volume pools. |
491|| `sfcc-payments` | `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` host (a `*.demandware.net` or SCAPI hostname — waiting confirmation from Mani) | Payment method metadata on every checkout page SSR | 10 | 5 s | 8 s | Called on every checkout page load; moderate frequency. Separate from `sfcc-scapi` because a checkout traffic spike must not consume SLAS connections. |
492|| `mulesoft` | `MULESOFT_BASE_URL` | Order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, GiveX balance check | 20 | 5 s | 10 s | Highest user-facing concurrency (My Account + PDP). GiveX balance calls carry payment credentials in the POST body — a slow MuleSoft response must not hold connections open and starve other pools. Highest cap reflects the broadest call surface. |
493|| `marketing-cloud-auth` | `<https://{subdomain}.auth.marketingcloudapis.com`> | Marketing Cloud client-credentials token exchange | 5 | 5 s | 15 s | User-triggered, infrequent; token cached at module scope for 15 min. Isolated so an MC outage cannot consume SFCC or MuleSoft connections. |
494|| `marketing-cloud-rest` | `<https://{subdomain}.rest.marketingcloudapis.com`> | Magic-link email send (passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 15 s | Same trigger as above; higher body timeout because email delivery APIs can respond slowly under load. |
495|| `google-places` | `<https://places.googleapis.com`> (Places API — New) | Address autocomplete at checkout (CFD-023, CFD-030, CFD-059) | 5 | 3 s | 5 s | Non-critical-path; graceful fallback to manual entry. Short timeouts ensure a Places API slowdown releases connections quickly. |
496|| `booxi` | Booxi base URL (TBD) | Boutique appointment read in My Account (CRM-165–167) | 5 | 3 s | 5 s | My Account only; non-critical-path within that page. |
497|
498|**Contentful:** The Contentful SDK (`contentful` v11) does not expose a `dispatcher` hook on its internal fetch calls, so connection isolation for Contentful is not achievable through this pattern. Primary mitigation is the graceful degradation rule in §12 (Render page without editorial content).
499|
500|---
501|
502|13. Testing Strategy
503|--------------------
504|
505|Three layers, no duplicated coverage — the cheapest layer that proves a behaviour wins.
506|
507|| Layer | Tool | Covers |
508|| --- | --- | --- |
509|| Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, isolated hooks |
510|| Component interaction | Storybook `play` | Single-component user interactions |
511|| E2E | Playwright | Full journeys, multi-region, integration boundaries |
512|
513|### 13.1 What is tested
514|
515|Failure paths that would be non-obvious or costly to debug: Contentful → component data mapping, locale / currency transforms, Global-e pricing / tax branching, checkout ownership, consent gating, cart mutations, optimistic-update rollback. Framework behaviour and pure visual rendering are not tested at this layer.
516|
517|### 13.2 E2E gherkin-first workflow
518|
519|Every Playwright spec starts as a Gherkin `.feature` file that Lead QA validates in plain English before any code is written. This prevents technically correct tests of the wrong behaviour.
520|
521|### 13.3 Multi-region fixtures
522|
523|E2E specs are parameterised by `SITE_ID` from day one — every journey runs across all 8 storefronts and 11 active locales, with site-specific `baseUrl`, currency, checkout owner, tax model, and consent default supplied by a fixture rather than hardcoded. (Because a test hardcoded to one region cannot be cheaply expanded later)
524|
525|### 13.4 Selector priority
526|
527|Tests select elements the way users and assistive tech perceive them: accessible selectors (role + name, label, visible text) first, semantic HTML attributes second (`alt`, `title`), `data-testid` only when nothing semantic applies. Tag/class/DOM-position selectors are not used. This doubles as a continuous accessibility check.
528|
529|---
530|
531|14. CI/CD & Environments
532|------------------------
533|
534|This section probably belong to a DevOps TSD, but will put here temporarily until we have one.
535|
536|### 14.1 Topology
537|
538|A six-tier environment topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → Stage → UAT → Prod**. Each tier (other than Local) has its own SFCC realm, Contentful environment, and MuleSoft connections. Ownership splits across three zones — Digital, IT/NewStore, and Shared (Digital + Business).
539|
540|| # | Tier | Owner | Purpose | Third-party availability | Deploy trigger |
541|| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
542|| 1 | **Local** | Digital | Feature build on developer machines | All services mocked (MSW stubs) | `npm start` |
543|| 2 | **Dev** | Digital | Integrated digital testing across all 6 storefronts, independent of NewStore | MuleSoft STG · NewStore Dev · Omneo STG · Narvar stub · Adyen sandbox | Merge to `develop` |
544|| 3 | **SIT** | IT / NewStore | NewStore SIT and regression on its own cadence | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Narvar STG · AP21 test | NewStore release cadence (parallel lane, non-blocking for Digital releases) |
545|| 4 | **Stage** (E2E) | Shared | End-to-end testing with all third parties live; time-boxed booked windows | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Omneo STG · Narvar STG · Adyen sandbox | Booked 2-week window |
546|| 5 | **UAT** | Shared | Business acceptance across all 6 regions | NewStore STG · Narvar STG · Omneo STG · Adyen sandbox | Business approval gate |
547|| 6 | **Prod** | Live | Production; AU canary then flag-flip to remaining regions | NewStore PROD · MuleSoft PROD · Omneo PROD · Narvar PROD · Adyen PROD | Release manager + canary gate |
548|
549|Stage is the **contractual performance-test environment** referenced in §9.3 — it mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle class, CDN/edge configuration, SFCC realm tier).
550|
551|### 14.2 Branch model
552|
553|GitFlow with explicit back-merges to keep `develop` aligned with production.
554|
555|| Branch | Branched from | Merges to |
556|| --- | --- | --- |
557|| `feature/*` | `develop` | `develop` |
558|| `fix/*` | `develop` | `develop` |
559|| `release/*` | `develop` | `main` **and** `develop` |
560|| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch (forward-merged to `develop` via the release back-merge) |
561|| `hotfix/*` | `main` | `main` **and** `develop` |
562|| `develop`, `main` | — | protected; PR-only |
563|
564|Release branches are supervised — code logic fixes go on a `fix/release-{version}-*` sub-branch rather than directly on the release branch. Releases and hotfixes always back-merge to `develop` so production fixes flow forward automatically.
565|
566|### 14.3 CI workflows
567|
568|**QA workflow (**`qa.yml`) — runs on every PR to `develop` and `release/**`. Code-correctness checks with no environment dependency:
569|
570|* Unit tests (Vitest)
571|* Storybook interaction tests (`play` functions) and component-level accessibility checks via `@storybook/addon-a11y` (`storybook test --ci`)
572|
573|**SIT gate (**`digital-sit.yml`) — runs on push/PR to `release/**`; on merge to `develop` it also deploys to the **Dev** environment (tier 2 in §14.1). Environment-dependent checks:
574|
575|* Playwright `p0` priority specs
576|* Bundle-size check against the ceilings in §9
577|* Contract tests against the MuleSoft OpenAPI specification
578|* Lighthouse CI thresholds (Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90)
579|* Trend gate against the LHCI history server
580|
581|### 14.4 Deployment
582|
583|Deployment is via Salesforce Managed Runtime. Each tier maps to its own MRT target:
584|
585|* **Dev** — deployed on merge to `develop`, gated on a clean SIT gate (§14.3)
586|* **SIT** — deployed on the NewStore release cadence, isolated from the Digital release path (failures do not block `release/**`)
587|* **Stage** — deployed on a booked 2-week window for full end-to-end testing with live third parties
588|* **UAT** — deployed for business acceptance; promotion requires Business sign-off
589|* **Prod** — release-manager-gated; AU canary first, then flag-flip to remaining regions
590|
591|Production deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through Stage and UAT.
592|
593|MRT deployment targets map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | stage | uat | production`.

> All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and run on a single SFCC realm with shared customer data. This determines how a shopper's session behaves when they cross storefronts (via the country / language selector or the mismatch slide-out):

> * **Session cookie is shared.** The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is first-party to the one domain, so it is presented on requests to any storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.

> * **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A SLAS token carries the site it was issued for, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context for the destination storefront. > * **Basket does not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency against its own pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency / pricebook boundary would produce incorrect pricing.
